title: Learned interatomic potential identifies a diamond-defect pathway
summary: A fine-tuned graph neural potential identified a two-stage formation pathway for a diamond di-interstitial absent from its training configurations. Selected density-functional calculations supported the pathway’s energetics. This is a computational defect-mechanism result, not an experimentally observed formation route.
ai_technology: Fine-tuned CHGNet graph neural interatomic potential
organization: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

evidence.tested: Training used 989 structures; the new di-interstitial pathway was generated without further training and checked with selected DFT single-point energies.
evidence.unknown: Checks support selected configurations, not a fully independently optimized or experimentally verified pathway. Correlated trajectory tests and approximate PBE energetics constrain accuracy. The separately discussed stepwise vacancy mechanism has prior literature precedent.
evidence.ai_role: The learned potential screens structures and reaction paths beyond its training defect configuration.

source_review.scope: Exact primary v1 front/history and complete physical computational Methods/Results; no later-version backdating.
